info.name: Payroll Breakdown
info.description:
Day-by-day payroll breakdown APIs.

Base URL: {{base_url}}
All routes are scoped under: /api/companies/:company_id/payrolls

Auth: Bearer token via Authorization header (verifyToken middleware)
Role: isManager minimum for GET, isAdmin for mutations

---

### What changed

Daily lines are a **frozen snapshot** taken at generation time, so the breakdown always matches what was generated regardless of later attendance edits. Rows now carry `attendance_status` and a plain-language `remarks` explaining the classification.

Two new day types — `half_day_unpaid_leave` and `not_employed` — and a corrected sandwich-leave rule. See the **Day Type Glossary** folder.

request.description:
Returns a day-by-day salary breakdown for a single payroll record.

Each day shows:
- day_type: present | absent | holiday | week_off | paid_leave | half_day_leave | unpaid_leave | half_day | comp_off | sandwich
- payable_amount: salary earned for that day
- deduction_amount: salary deducted for that day
- net_day_amount: payable + overtime for that day
- is_sandwich: true if the day was caught by the sandwich leave rule

item.name: 2. Get Breakdown — All Employees in Period

request.description:
Returns daily breakdowns for every employee in the given payroll period.

Employees with errors (missing salary structure, DB issues) are returned in the `failed` array — other employees still succeed.

Useful for the admin review screen before approving/paying payroll.

request.description: Token belongs to a role below isManager (e.g. a regular employee). The authorizeRoles middleware rejects.
company_id in the URL does not match the company_id in the verified token — validateTenant rejects.

### Day type glossary

Every row in `daily_breakdown` carries a `day_type`:

| `day_type` | Meaning | Paid |
|---|---|---|
| `present` | Full day worked | full |
| `half_day` | Worked under the shift's half-day threshold | half |
| `absent` | No attendance record, or marked absent | none |
| `paid_leave` | Approved leave on a paid leave type | full |
| `half_day_leave` | Half leave + half worked | full |
| `unpaid_leave` | Approved leave on an unpaid type | none |
| `half_day_unpaid_leave` | **NEW** — half-day unpaid leave | half |
| `week_off` | Rest day per the shift | full |
| `holiday` | Company or branch holiday | full |
| `comp_off` | Earned comp-off — **never** swallowed by a sandwich | full |
| `sandwich` | Off-day bridged by full-day absences either side | none |
| `not_employed` | **NEW** — before `joining_date` / after `exit_date` | none |

`not_employed` is **not** an absence. Style it neutrally, never red — docking someone for days before they joined and calling it absence is a support call waiting to happen.

---

### Sandwich leave — what changed

A sandwich is a run of bridgeable off-days flanked on **both** sides by a full day of lost pay.

- **Bookends must be full-day losses.** Previously any deductible day counted, and a half day lands in that set — so *half day Friday + half day Monday* made the weekend unpaid. It no longer does.
- **comp-off is never bridgeable** — it was earned by working.
- **Holidays are opt-in** via `sandwich_applies_to`. Most policies bridge week-offs only.
- **The bridge is length-capped** (`sandwich_max_bridge_days`), so one absence either side of a long shutdown cannot zero out the whole stretch.
- A run touching either edge of the period is never sandwiched — the neighbouring period is not visible, so it is not guessed.

All configurable per company: `GET /payroll-runs/settings`.

---

### New fields on each row

- `attendance_status` — the raw attendance status behind the classification
- `remarks` — **why** the day was classified this way, in plain language: *"Worked 3h, below the 4h half-day threshold"*, *"Sandwiched between full-day absences"*, *"Before joining date"*. Show it; this is what stops the "why was I docked?" ticket.

### Invariants you can rely on

- `pay_fraction + deduct_fraction === 1` on **every** row
- `Σ payable_amount + Σ deduction_amount === gross_salary`
- `net_salary === Σ payable_amount + Σ overtime_amount`

### New summary fields

`sandwich_days`, `not_employed_days`, `payable_days`, `total_half_days`, `total_week_off`, `total_comp_off`, plus `stored_net_salary`, `final_net_salary` and `is_stale` — when `is_stale` is true the stored figures no longer match the adjustments, so call `POST /payrolls/:id/recalculate`.

### Timezone

Day-of-week is computed in **UTC**. It previously read a UTC-parsed date with local-time getters, so on any server west of UTC every week-off landed a day early and the whole classification shifted.
